City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Agency, Community Development Financing Authority, Public Improvement Corporation, and Library Board of Trustees*
November 20, 2006
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, Community Development Agency, Community Development Financing Authority, Public Improvement Corporation, and Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor MacLean at 05:00 p.m. , on November 20, 2006, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on November 15, 2006, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
CALL TO ORDER—CITY COUNCIL, COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AGENCY, COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT FINANCING AUTHORITY, PUBLIC IMPROVEMENT CORPORATION, AND LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES

Council Member/Agency Member Kelley
Council Member/Agency Member Ledesma

None

Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Irwin Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services
William P. Curley III, City Attorney
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
RECESS
Mayor MacLean recessed the meeting at 5:01 p.m. The City Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all Council Members present.

PRESENTATIONS

Presentation to the City of Financial Reporting Awards Received During 2006 from the Government Finance Officers Association of the United States and Canada and the California Society of Municipal Finance Officers
Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented Mayor MacLean with the GFOA and CSMFO Awards and praised the Administrative Services Department staff for their efforts to help the City achieve these prestigious State and National awards for the City budget.
P2.
Recognize the Mission Viejo Tennis Center Men’s Senior 3.5 USTA Tennis Team for Winning the Senior Sectional Championships
Presented certificates of commendation to Team Captain Brian Gruner and members of the Mission Viejo Senior Tennis Team.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Steven Guess, M.V.:
spoke in support of residential board and care facilities and expressed concern about the potential for limiting the number of these facilities in the City.
Dave Gove, M.V.:
displayed items left at his doorstep by solicitors and asked the City Council to revisit the Ordinance relating to canvassing and solicitation within City limits.
Dale Sandore, M.V.:
discussed an article in the Orange County Register regarding 50" plasma traffic video monitors proposed for installation at Mission Viejo library and at city hall and expressed concern with the expenditure.
Allan Pilger, M.V.:
echoed Mr. Sandore’s comments regarding the City’s proposed traffic video monitors and asked the public to decide the value.
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.:
stated that the three majestic pines scheduled for destruction at the YMCA must be saved and asked the City and the Planning Commission to allow for public comment before the trees are destroyed.
Linda Hernani, M.V.:
stated that the property at the YMCA is very unique, in part because of the beautiful pine trees. Asked the City Council to look at a modified plan and come up with a solution to protect the trees that are scheduled for destruction.
Chuck Costello, Chairman of the YMCA Board of Directors, M.V.:
stated that the YMCA has no involvement in the destruction of trees and expressed concern with the project delay which could conflict with their summer aquatics program.

STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Reports
25.
Ferrocarril Landslide Updates (0400-10)
City Engineer Rich Schlesinger presented an update on the Ferrocarril landslide.
City Manager Dennis Wilberg provided an update on the traffic situation near Newhart School and the request from a resident for installation of an access gate off of Pasatiempo. That resident has submitted a petition with only 19 of the 52 affected homeowners signing in support of an access gate. Mr. Wilberg stated that the City prefers 2/3 of the affected residents support the proposal before implementing any extraordinary traffic control measures and that he will be in contact with the resident to find out if other homeowners have signed the petition since submission of the first draft.
Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein provided an update of the CUSD audit.
City Attorney’s Reports
Managers, members of the legislature, and owners of assisted living facilities to come together and seek solutions.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS
26.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended (AB 1234) (0480-70)
Council Members acknowledged the accuracy of their event and activities calendars as presented in the staff report.
City Attorney Bill Curley Asked the City Council Members to mark March 2, 2007, on their calendars for a meeting regarding the issue of group housing. The City of Newport Beach has scheduled a conference for City Council Members, City The City Council Member Kelley Reminded concerned CUSD residents that there will be a meeting on November 28, 2006, at the Capistrano Unified School District administration office for presentation of the numbers and the funding mechanisms for the new administration building. Outlined her attendance at the Trauma Intervention Program "Heroes with Heart" banquet that honored the TIP volunteers who help those who are experiencing tragedy in their lives. Stated that this is a valuable program and those interested in learning more can contact her or Sandy Hill, TIP Manager. Announced that Grace Community Church will bring back their live nativity program on December 3 from 6:00 to 7:30 p.m. and she encouraged residents to mark their calendars. Thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for hosting a great holiday boutique last Saturday and announced that Santa Claus will arrive in Mission Viejo on Sunday, November 26, 2006, at 5:00 p.m. at the four corners. This will kick off the holiday events planned by the Activities Committee and she reminded those looking for a worthwhile volunteer opportunity to contact her or call 830-7066 for more information. Thanked Home Depot for their generous donation of six Christmas trees for the Santa’s Workshop display.
Council Member Ledesma
Wished residents and his colleagues a Happy Thanksgiving and encouraged everyone to take the time to reflect on the things we have to be thankful for in this nation and this community.
Council Member Reavis
Thanked City Manager Dennis Wilberg for his leadership and guidance with the Orange County City Managers’ Association “White Paper” which outlines the OCCMA’s recommended structure and inter-relationship for the Orange County Division, League of California Cities and the Orange County Council of Governments. Discussed her attendance at the Marine Corps 231st birthday ball in Camp Pendleton and announced that the Marines and their families are very grateful that Mission Viejo has adopted the First Battalion. The City is still accepting donations of food and gift certificates for the Battalion for Thanksgiving and toys/gifts for Christmas. Announced that the new Walgreens store on Estanciero is now open. Stated that the book “Mission Viejo, The Ageless Land” would make a great holiday gift and residents can purchase a copy at City Hall. Outlined her attendance at Metrolink’s toy train arrival, the fundraiser at the Shops at Mission Viejo, and Veteran’s Day services at the El Toro cemetery and here in Mission Viejo. Stated that the City’s hero flag display was one of the most moving exhibits she has ever witnessed and for those who were unable to view it, MVTV is airing a rerun of the event. Thanked staff for putting together a grand and respectful ceremony for the Veterans in the Country and in the City.
Mayor Pro Tempore Ury
Asked staff to place an item on the next Agenda, under his comments, regarding the OCTA MIS study. Wished everyone a happy Thanksgiving and safe travels.
Mayor MacLean
Announced that Mission Viejo High School and Trabuco Hills High School marching bands competed in the Western Band Association Championships in Fresno and both high schools earned 2nd place in their respective divisions. The bands then went on to the finals competition where MVHS finished second and THHS finished seventh overall. Congratulated both bands and high schools on their success. Stated that Council Member Kelley was one of the MC’s at the TIP “Heroes With Heart” banquet and thanked her for the work she does with that organization. Announced that holiday displays are being assembled at the four corners and that Santa Claus will arrive there by fire truck on Sunday. Reminded residents to drive safely and take a little extra time as they travel over the holidays.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 8:07 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor MacLean adjourned the meeting to December 4, 2006, at 5:00 p.m.
